subject: Forecast category revamp: definitions, hygiene sprint & mandatory training
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 08:32:00 -0800
Subject: Forecast category revamp: definitions, hygiene sprint & mandatory training

Team —

Quick heads-up: Finance ran a short audit of our Q4 forecast and found too much variance across "Commit" and "Best Case" assignments. This is causing noisy roll-ups and added rework during weekly commit reviews. We need a short, coordinated change to reduce ambiguity and get everyone aligned before the year close.

What I'm proposing: a focused "hygiene sprint" next week plus an hour of mandatory training for all AEs/AMs and Sales Ops. The changes are intentionally conservative — mostly clarifying the boundaries between Pipeline / Best Case / Commit and adding a simple commit-confidence rubric (P0–P3).

Please review the two attachments (slide deck + mapping CSV) before our kickoff: 1) rationale & new definitions, 2) one-line examples and a mapping you can paste into your team notes.

High level timeline:
- Nov 16: new definitions go live in the handbook (read-only).
- Nov 17–19: hygiene sprint window (make stage updates, annotate deals with P0–P3 confidence).
- Nov 20 @ 10:00 PT: mandatory training (45 min) + Q&A — calendar invite incoming.

Immediate asks (by EOD Nov 16):
- Everyone: skim the slide deck.
- Managers (Marissa, Karthik, Lauren): identify top 15 deals per rep that must be re-reviewed during the sprint.
- Ben: can Sales Ops push an export with stage-change history so teams can prioritize?

Why this matters: small upfront time now will cut down manual commit corrections during forecast calls and reduce surprise churn at month-end. I know this is aggressive; I appreciate the team's grit.

Attachments: forecast-category-change-slide-deck.pdf (summary + examples), commit-mapping-spreadsheet.csv (editable mapping for your notes)

Thanks —
Logan
Logan Wright
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the note, Logan — this looks helpful. Quick questions after a first pass through the deck: 

1) The P0–P3 confidence rubric is clear, but do we plan to store that confidence as a custom property on the deal or as a stage suffix? My recommendation is a custom property (deal.confidence) so it survives stage renames.

2) For the "top 15 deals per rep" ask, I'll work with each manager to produce that list. Do we want SDR-owned opportunities included, or stick to rep-owned only?

3) If Sales Ops can provide the export Ben mentioned, it would help prioritize deals that toggled stages more than twice in the last 30 days.

I'll block time with my managers and share a combined spreadsheet by EOD Nov 16.

—Marissa

- Edge cases: For multi-owner deals where AM+CS both update forecast, the owner of record (closest to renewal/expansion exec) gets the vote unless the deal is marked as "joint" — see slide 6.

Calendar: training invite sent for Nov 20 10:00 PT (45 min). Please mark as "required" for AEs, AMs, Sales Ops, and Revenue Managers. We'll record and publish notes for those who absolutely cannot attend.
